subject: Dylan Rivera — final interview debrief and hire recommendation
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Gupta <asha@talentco.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dylan Rivera — final interview debrief and hire recommendation

Team —

Thanks for interviewing Dylan this morning. Quick ask: please drop your numerical score + 1–2 line rationale in the attached scorecard (or reply inline) by EOD Pacific today. We have a tight slot with hiring to confirm next steps tomorrow.

Context / hiring bar highlights:
- Role: Senior Inference Engineer (IC4)
- Interview loop included system design (Marissa), performance/opt (Mina), and culture/peer match (Logan).
- Candidate background: 6 years in infra, recently at FlowScale (see resume attached).

Attachments: Dylan_Rivera_Resume.pdf | scorecard-dylan-rivera.xlsx

If you have a strong thumbs-up or a veto please flag in your reply — I want explicit calls rather than silent defaults.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Hiring Partner, Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dylan Rivera — final interview debrief and hire recommendation

Sergio —

Score (out of 5): 4
Quick rationale: Strong design thinking for distributed KV cache and clear tradeoffs on consistency vs latency. Asked good follow‑ups on failure modes. Felt slightly light on quantifying tail latency strategies for 99.9% SLOs — would want to probe more if we were shipping tomorrow.

Notes (snip of my scorecard):
- System design: 4/5 — sound architecture, missed an optimization for hot key sharding that I expected.
- Ownership/communication: 5/5 — very concise.
- Team fit: 4/5.

No veto. I lean hire if we can pair for a short follow-up on tail latency techniques during onboarding.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff SW Eng (Serving)
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dylan Rivera — final interview debrief and hire recommendation

Sergio / team —

Score (out of 5): 3
Quick rationale: Good instincts on quantization/ops, but the candidate struggled to articulate concrete approaches for KV-cache eviction under mixed workload; also unclear on debugging noisy GPU outliers. Given the role's emphasis on production performance, I have reservations.

Key excerpt from my notes: "Candidate described LRU-style eviction but didn't discuss TTL + hot-key amplification or telemetry-driven eviction thresholds. Wanted more evidence of running A/B latency experiments in production."

Veto? Not an outright veto, but I recommend a short technical homework or a 30m follow-up with me focusing on tail-latency experiments before we extend an offer.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

All —

Consolidating the inputs: Marissa 4, Mina 3, Logan 4. I pulled the scorecard into the Greenhouse record (link below) and added a short summary. My read: solid candidate, small gaps on production performance depth but high coachability and excellent cross-team communication.

Recommendation: move to an offer with the caveat of a 30m technical follow-up with Mina as part of the pre‑start checklist (or as a condition of offer if hiring team prefers). If we don't want conditional steps, we can instead send a short take‑home focused on tail-latency/eviction strategies.

Final call: Sergio — do you want to greenlight an offer (level IC4, comp band B3) with Mina follow-up, or hold? I don't think this needs a full loop repeat.

Attachments added to GH: scorecard-dylan-rivera.xlsx
Greenhouse: https://greenhouse.example/candidate/12345

—Logan
